items.title: LMCache integration ignores per-request cache_salt: external storage keys are token-only, breaking tenant isolation
items.body:
Measured on SGLang 0.5.18 + LMCache 0.5.4 (MP mode: `lmcache server` daemon + `--enable-lmcache --lmcache-config-file`).

## The defect

SGLang's radix tree honours `cache_salt` per request — but the LMCache storage path does not, by SGLang's own documented contract (`srt/mem_cache/radix_cache.py:59-80`):

> It namespaces the in-process radix tree and external KV events; external L3/remote storage keys remain token-only and are outside this contract.

With LMCache enabled, that contract means two **different tenants** (different `cache_salt`) with the same prompt produce identical storage keys and share cached prefixes — a cross-tenant timing/compute side channel, measured end-to-end: a second account's identical prefix served from the first account's cache (1198 ms) against a 3430 ms recompute baseline.

## Where the salt is dropped

The scheduler has the salt in scope on every LMCache call, but the handoff cannot carry it:

- LOOKUP: `srt/mem_cache/storage/lmcache/lmc_radix_cache.py:223` calls `lookup_kv(token_ids, req.rid)` with `key.cache_salt` in scope but not forwarded (`:236` even copies it into the load-back marker).
- STORE: `cache_finished_req` (`:470-489`) has `req.cache_salt` (`:475`) but `StoreMetadata` has no salt field.
- LMCache's wire key `IPCCacheServerKey` **has** a `cache_salt` field (default `""`), and LMCache's vLLM integration populates it — only the SGLang path drops it (LMCache issue filed: LMCache/LMCache#4825).

## The ask

Carry `cache_salt` across the SGLang→LMCache handoff so the "external keys are token-only" contract can be narrowed to "keys are token+salt". Per-tenant `cache_salt` is SGLang's own recommended mechanism for cache isolation on multi-tenant serving (its docs ask for a value "protected from access by 3rd parties"); with external storage enabled, that recommendation currently does not hold.

items.title: [Feature] Tuning / per-GPU config for DSv4 top-k v2 cluster launch plan (kClusterFloor / kNumPersistentClusters / kCandidates)
items.body:
## Summary

The DSv4 top-k v2 cooperative-cluster kernel (`python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/deepseek_v4/topk_v2.cuh`) selects its launch plan from **hardcoded, B200/sm100-derived `constexpr` values**. There is no benchmark harness and no per-GPU tuned-config / autotune path for these parameters, even though the code itself flags the plan as tunable. This is the one piece of the DSA decode path that has no tuning story, in contrast to fused-MoE and DeepGEMM which both do.

## The hardcoded launch plan (main)

In `topk_v2.cuh`:

```cpp
constexpr uint32_t kClusterFloor = 65536;                 // L58
constexpr uint32_t kClusterMaxBatch = 512;                // L59
constexpr uint32_t kNumPersistentClusters = 15 * kOccupancy;  // L60  (15 == B200 one-wave cluster count)
...
// L379: "cap = pool size only fits the shortest (~98K, one-wave) bucket. (Plan is tunable.)"
constexpr Pair kCandidates[] = { {65536,30},{98304,48},{131072,60},{196608,80},{262144,112},{393216,128} };  // L384
...
constexpr uint32_t kClusterFloorSmall = 32768;            // L545
constexpr uint32_t kSmallBatchLowFloor = 15;              // L546
```

`kNumPersistentClusters = 15 * kOccupancy` is literally the B200 single-wave cluster count; the `kCandidates` `{threshold, max_batch_size}` plan table and the two cluster floors are B200-tuned magic numbers. The `(Plan is tunable.)` comment states the intent, but nothing exposes it — no env var, no config file, no autotune. On any non-B200 SM (different SM count / occupancy / L2 / cluster-launch behavior), these are heuristics, not tuned values.

#35095 (adaptive small-batch cluster split) improves the dispatch and explicitly notes the split caps are *"B200/sm100 autotune values scaled by SM count at runtime"* — i.e. still baked B200 constants scaled by a scalar, not values tuned for the target device. That PR makes the split adaptive; it does not give the plan a tuning mechanism.

## Why this matters (measured)

On B200 the plan is fine — decode top-k stays cheap. Measured decode share (v0.5.17, TP8, graph-off, compute-relative i.e. after removing the all-reduce spin floor):

| model | K | top-k @32K | top-k @1M | kernel |
|-------|---|-----------|-----------|--------|
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash | 512 | 1.4% | 4.1% | `topk_small_batch_kernel` |
| DeepSeek-V4-Pro | 1024 | 2.1% | 4.8% | `topk_small_batch_kernel` |

`topk_small_batch_kernel` (the cooperative `__cluster_dims__` kernel) is the only decode top-k path, and per-launch cost scales sub-linearly with context because the persistent-cluster pool is sized for the B200 wave. The concern is portability: the same constants on a device with a different SM/occupancy profile will either under-fill the pool (idle clusters) or oversubscribe it (extra waves), and there is currently no supported way to retune without editing and recompiling the `.cuh`.

## Asymmetry with existing tuning infra

- fused-MoE: `benchmark/kernels/fused_moe_triton/tuning_fused_moe_triton.py`, `tuning_client.py`, tuned config JSONs.
- DeepGEMM: `benchmark/kernels/deepseek/benchmark_deepgemm_fp8_gemm*.py`.
- DSA indexer scoring: `benchmark/kernels/deepseek/benchmark_cute_dsl_fp8_paged_mqa_logits.py`.
- **DSv4 top-k v2 cluster kernel: no benchmark, no tuning script, no per-device config.**

## Proposed feature

1. A `benchmark/kernels/deepseek/benchmark_topk_v2.py` that sweeps (batch, max_seq_len, K, page_size) and reports the cluster-vs-streaming crossover and pool occupancy — so the plan can be measured per device.
2. Make the launch plan device-tunable rather than a compile-time `constexpr`: either a small tuned-config lookup keyed by device name (mirroring the MoE config JSONs) selecting `{kClusterFloor, kClusterFloorSmall, kNumPersistentClusters, kCandidates}`, or a documented runtime override, with the current B200 values as the default entry.

Happy to contribute this; it slots on top of #35095 (whose split caps would become the first tuned entry) and is independent of the correctness issue #35257.

items.title: [Bug] Spec V2 paths no longer emit speculative-decoding OpenTelemetry spans
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists on the latest `main` revision checked below.
- [x] This report includes an exact revision, environment, and a minimal reproducible source check.
- [x] This is a bug report rather than a general question.
- [x] This report is in English.

### Describe the bug

PR #19545 added per-request OpenTelemetry stages for speculative decoding. On current `main` (`e51a3ae65e3401b21de860c90a64102133d2d6a6`), the Spec V2 paths no longer preserve that tracing contract:

- EAGLE v2 has no calls to the request timing setters. Its `spec_stage_span(draft / draft_extend)` scopes are backed by `profile_range`, i.e. profiler/NVTX ranges rather than per-request OpenTelemetry spans. As a result, the current EAGLE path cannot emit the `spec_draft` or `spec_verify` request spans; `spec_draft_extend` was removed entirely.
- NGRAM still calls the `spec_draft` start/end setters, but the target-verify/sample path never calls `set_spec_verify_start_time` or `set_spec_verify_end_time`. Therefore it cannot emit `spec_verify`, `num_correct_drafts`, or the compatibility `accepted_tokens` attribute.
- `RequestStage.SPEC_VERIFY` and both verify setters remain in `req_time_stats.py`, but have zero call sites in the current tree.

Relevant current-main code:

- [`req_time_stats.py` keeps the request-span setters](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/e51a3ae65e3401b21de860c90a64102133d2d6a6/python/sglang/srt/observability/req_time_stats.py#L664-L701)
- [NGRAM records draft timing, then performs verify/sample without verify timing](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/e51a3ae65e3401b21de860c90a64102133d2d6a6/python/sglang/srt/speculative/ngram_worker.py#L429-L506)
- [EAGLE v2 uses `spec_stage_span` around draft/draft-extend](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/e51a3ae65e3401b21de860c90a64102133d2d6a6/python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py#L1238-L1267), while [`spec_stage_span` returns `profile_range`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/e51a3ae65e3401b21de860c90a64102133d2d6a6/python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_utils.py#L697-L701)

The loss appears to have happened across three later changes: #25464 removed EAGLE v1 without migrating its per-request OTel hooks, #17260 removed the NGRAM verify hooks during its V2 migration, and #28133 subsequently removed the now-dead draft-extend request stage. The closed tracing roadmap #13511 still marks speculative-decoding tracing complete via #19545.

Expected behavior: when request tracing is enabled, current speculative workers should preserve a defined set of per-request draft/verify stage spans and the per-request accepted/correct-draft count. Tracing-disabled execution should not add per-request tracing-only work.

Before preparing a current-main patch, could maintainers confirm the intended Spec V2 contract—especially which EAGLE v2 operations should map to `spec_draft`, `spec_verify`, and possibly `spec_draft_extend`? I can then add focused regression tests and a small implementation against that agreed boundary. This is a narrower current-main follow-up to the superseded broad attempt in #23197.

### Reproduction

From an exact checkout of current `main`:

```bash
git checkout e51a3ae65e3401b21de860c90a64102133d2d6a6
git grep -n -F set_spec_verify_start_time -- python
git grep -n -F set_spec_verify_end_time -- python
git grep -n -F set_spec_draft_start_time -- python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py
git grep -n -F SPEC_DRAFT_EXTEND -- python
```

The first two commands return only the method definitions in `req_time_stats.py`; the EAGLE and draft-extend searches return no matches. Inspecting the active NGRAM control flow shows draft timing at lines 436-438 and target verification at lines 443-506 with no verify timing calls.

This is a source-level call-site reproduction; it does not require a model or GPU. By control-flow inspection, enabling request tracing cannot create the missing spans because the active workers never invoke the request-span setters.

### Environment

- Repository revision: `e51a3ae65e3401b21de860c90a64102133d2d6a6` (current `main` at report time)
- Reproduction type: deterministic source/call-site check; no model, GPU, or SGLang runtime import required
- Model / GPU / CUDA: N/A
- Host used for the commands: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS under WSL2, Linux `6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2`, x86_64
- Python: 3.12.3 (not used by the reproduction)
- Git: 2.43.0
- `python3 -m sglang.check_env`: N/A because this reproducer does not import or run SGLang; host runtime state cannot restore deleted call sites

If maintainers prefer an exporter-level runtime trace in addition to the deterministic source check, I can add one from an appropriate EAGLE/NGRAM GPU environment before proposing a fix.

items.title: [Bug] Qwen3.8-Flash-Next QSA + NEXTN decode graph silently corrupts output on GB10 TP2
items.body:
## Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues and found no report of this silent semantic-corruption mode.
- [ ] The bug has been revalidated on current SGLang main. The tested image is pinned to the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next day-zero stack described below.
- [x] A public qualification harness and controlled eager/graph comparison are included.
- [x] This report is in English.

## Describe the bug

On 2x GB10 with TP2, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next QSA + NEXTN decode CUDA graphs can return HTTP 200 and substantially higher throughput while silently producing semantically invalid output. We observed two independent failures during the same Graph candidate boot:

1. a 1,024-token non-looping essay test degenerates into repeated punctuation (`!`);
2. an approximately 25K-token prompt containing four ordered markers fails to retrieve the markers and also degenerates into repeated punctuation.

The same model, prompts, and runtime pass both gates with decode CUDA graphs disabled. This is not a timeout, OOM, or server crash. It is silent output corruption and therefore cannot be detected by health checks or throughput benchmarks.

This issue reports only the silent-corruption A/B. It is distinct from #37052, an independent external report of invalid-probability asserts and rank termination. A preceding local overlap-related crash is summarized in the companion repository, but this issue does not claim that the two incidents share one root cause.

## Controlled A/B

Common configuration:

```text
hardware: 2x ASUS Ascent GX10 / NVIDIA GB10 (SM121), TP2 over RoCEv2
model: RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4
SGLang base: d91c3682b Qwen3.8-Flash-Next development image plus SM121 QSA/M-RoPE fixes
QSA draft-extend compatibility fix: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37110
dense FP4: flashinfer_cudnn
MoE: flashinfer_cutlass
NEXTN: steps/topk/draft = 3/1/4
Mamba state: float32
linear/GDN backend: triton
max running requests: 2
context: 262144
radix cache: disabled
overlap schedule: disabled
```

Only the graph profile changed:

```text
Eager control:
  --disable-cuda-graph

Graph candidate:
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 2
  --disable-cuda-graph-padding
  --disable-prefill-cuda-graph
  --speculative-attention-mode decode
```

Results:

| Profile | 2,048-token code decode | 1,024-token loop gate | ~25K four-marker retrieval |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Eager | 41.60 / 42.39 / 42.86 tok/s | pass | pass |
| Decode Graph | 50.66 tok/s observed | fail: punctuation repetition | fail: markers missing / punctuation repetition |

The eager control also completed a 16,384-token continuous generation at 48.01 tok/s and then served a short request. Both ranks remained at zero restarts.

## Evidence scope

- The Eager throughput row contains three measurements.
- `50.66 tok/s` is one observed Graph throughput measurement, not a distribution.
- Both semantic failures occurred in one controlled Graph candidate boot. Cross-boot frequency has not yet been measured.
- No OOM, container restart, CUDA assert, or NCCL exit occurred in this semantic-failure run.
- The original result JSON was not preserved as a public artifact. The hardened public harness below is the reproducible gate, not a claim that the historical output has been independently replayed.
- The issue has not been re-run on the latest `qwen4-main-squashed` head or current main.

## Reproduction

The launcher, immutable environment identities, and qualification harness are pinned in companion commit `29198ba1317d1452706a5915f32bbedac919f7b7`:

https://github.com/hellojiaru/qwen38-flash-next-dual-gb10/tree/29198ba1317d1452706a5915f32bbedac919f7b7

The launcher defaults to Eager and guards the rejected Graph profile. Build the pinned image and configure both isolated test nodes as documented in the repository.

Run the Eager control worker-first:

```bash
./start-node.sh start 1 eager
./start-node.sh start 0 eager
python tools/qualify.py --base http://127.0.0.1:8918/v1 --long-tokens 25000 > eager-qualification.json
```

Stop both test ranks, set `ALLOW_REJECTED_PROFILE=1` in `.env` on both isolated nodes, then run the Graph candidate worker-first:

```bash
./start-node.sh start 1 graph-unsafe
./start-node.sh start 0 graph-unsafe
python tools/qualify.py --base http://127.0.0.1:8918/v1 --long-tokens 25000 > graph-qualification.json
```

The harness verifies arithmetic, tool name and JSON arguments, a synthetic vision fixture, reasoning plus the correct final answer, long non-looping output, ordered marker retrieval, and exact bounded responses. It rejects long repeated character/token runs.

The client harness cannot prove process stability. Reproducers should also record both ranks' restart count, `OOMKilled`, scheduler/NCCL errors, and kernel Xid events before and after each profile.

## Expected behavior

Decode CUDA graphs may change performance but must preserve the eager path's token semantics. If the graph path is unsupported for QSA + NEXTN on this stack, startup should fail closed or the graph path should be disabled rather than returning HTTP success with corrupted content.

## Notes

- BF16 Mamba state and a locally enabled FlashInfer GDN path caused separate semantic failures and are not part of this report.
- The companion repository CI is static validation only; it does not run the model or dual-node hardware.
- A current-head reproduction, raw eager/graph JSON outputs, and repeated Graph boots would materially strengthen this report.

items.title: [Bug] GLM-5.3-Flash on RTX PRO 6000 (sm_120): two DSA backend blockers after the deep_gemm NameError
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

Serving `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` on **8x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120)** fails at
startup. After working around the known `deep_gemm` NameError (#29738), **two further blockers**
appear, both in the DSA attention backend. Neither is reachable by configuration.

This mirrors #33194 (same model family, SM80/Ampere): the DSA/MHC kernels appear to assume
**datacenter-class** GPUs (sm_90 Hopper / sm_100 Blackwell DC). sm_120 is a workstation part with
**half the shared memory and no TMEM/tcgen05**.

### Environment

```
GPU            8x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120)
shared mem     102,400 B / SM   (H200 sm_90: 227 KB)
driver         610.43.02
image          lmsysorg/sglang:glm-5.3-flash   (base aa8c950a3d)
model          zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash  (index_kpool=4, 45 layers, 288 experts)
launch         --tp-size 8 --data-parallel-size 8 --enable-dp-attention
               --expert-parallel-size 8 --disable-shared-experts-fusion
               --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16
               --mm-enable-dp-encoder --context-length 1048576
```

### Blocker 0 (pre-existing, #29738) — triggered automatically on sm_120

`configurer.py` deliberately excludes sm_120:

```python
# python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/configurer.py
# "DeepGEMM requires TMEM/tcgen05 (SM100+datacenter), not available on SM120"
if sm_version == 120:
    return False        # -> ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM = False
                        # -> entrypoint.py:19 `if ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM: import deep_gemm` is skipped
```

but `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM` is hardware-independent:

```python
# python/sglang/srt/environ.py
SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM = EnvBool(True)   # always True
```

so `mhc.py` still takes the deep_gemm branch and `entrypoint.py` calls it unguarded:

```
NameError: name 'deep_gemm' is not defined
  at srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/entrypoint.py  tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm()
  <- kernels/ops/layernorm/mhc.py  mhc_pre
  <- srt/models/glm5_next.py  hc_attn_pre
```

Measured on this host: `ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM=False` while `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM=True`.

**On sm_120 these two flags are always inconsistent** — #29738 required setting an env manually;
here it happens out of the box. Suggest gating `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM` on
`ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM`, or guarding the call site.

**Workaround:** `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM=0` (takes the non-deep_gemm branch in `mhc_pre`).
This works — and exposes the next two blockers.

### Blocker 1 — auto-selected `trtllm` DSA decode backend is unsupported on sm_120

```
Set DSA backends for bfloat16 KV Cache: prefill=flashmla_sparse, decode=trtllm
Capture cuda graph failed: Error in function 'TllmGenFmhaRunner'
  at /workspace/include/flashinfer/trtllm/fmha/fmhaRunner.cuh:37: Unsupported architecture
```

The auto-selector picks `trtllm` for Blackwell, but the TRT-LLM Gen FMHA kernel only supports
sm_100. `prefill=flashmla_sparse` itself passed — the failure is decode-side only.

### Blocker 2 — `tilelang` needs more shared memory than sm_120 has

Forcing both ends to tilelang (the combination used successfully on H20, and the one required by
the fp8-KV gate in #36904):

```
Set DSA backends for bfloat16 KV Cache: prefill=tilelang, decode=tilelang
tvm.error.InternalError: Failed to set the allowed dynamic shared memory size to 206848
```

```
requested   206,848 B  = 202 KB
available   102,400 B  = 100 KB   (hardware limit on sm_120)
```

This is a hard hardware limit, not configuration. It also means the **fp8 KV path of #36904 is
unreachable on sm_120**, since that gate requires tilelang on both ends.

### Reproduction

```bash
docker run --rm --gpus all --network host --ipc host --shm-size 32g \
  -v /path/to/GLM-5.3-Flash:/model:ro \
  -e SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM=0 \
  lmsysorg/sglang:glm-5.3-flash \
  python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /model --trust-remote-code \
    --tp-size 8 --data-parallel-size 8 --enable-dp-attention --expert-parallel-size 8 \
    --disable-shared-experts-fusion --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm \
    --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 --mm-enable-dp-encoder --context-length 1048576
```

### Questions

1. Is sm_120 (RTX PRO 6000 / RTX 5090 class) intended to be supported for GLM-5.3-Flash?
2. If yes, is there a DSA backend combination that fits within 100 KB shared memory?
   `prefill=flashmla_sparse` works; which decode backends are validated on sm_120?
3. Should `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM` default be derived from `ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM`
   so the sm_120 exclusion is self-consistent?

items.title: [Bug] Pretokenized image requests can crash GLM MRoPE with a stale retokenized mask
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no existing report.
- [x] The vulnerable code is present on current `main`.
- [x] This report includes a minimal reproduction and affected revisions.
- [x] This is a bug report, not a general question.
- [x] This report is in English.

### Describe the bug

Originally reported by @dzorlu in [this comment on #36833](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36833#issuecomment-5466686528), with a [minimal fix and workload reproduction](https://github.com/nanjiangwill/sglang/pull/1).

For a pretokenized image request, SGLang can pass two sequences with different provenance to GLM MRoPE:

- `input_ids`: the client's exact IDs, restored by `SGLANG_MM_AVOID_RETOKENIZE` after image-token expansion;
- `attention_mask`: produced by the HF processor over `decode(input_ids)` re-tokenized.

Decode followed by tokenization is not length-preserving for noncanonical token sequences. For example, two separately sampled newline tokens can re-tokenize as one combined newline token. GLM MRoPE then indexes exact IDs of length `N+1` with a mask of length `N` and raises `IndexError`.

This is easier to hit in long multi-turn RL because sampled IDs are repeatedly reused as context. Short, single-turn VLM tests generally start with canonical IDs and do not expose it.

The issue is not specific to the Miles branch:

- current `main` restores exact IDs in [`base_processor.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/512df615debca0240addeacedf19c28f0fc18c45/python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py#L1702-L1739), then passes the processor mask in [`glm4v.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/512df615debca0240addeacedf19c28f0fc18c45/python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/glm4v.py#L102-L113);
- the same pattern is present in the GLM-5.3 implementation in [#36507](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36507): [exact-ID restoration](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/7fa1924c04487feffc3f5f111a424ec1f0b22362/python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py#L1658-L1695) followed by the [retokenized mask](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/7fa1924c04487feffc3f5f111a424ec1f0b22362/python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/glm4v.py#L553-L564).

Although RL submits many rollouts concurrently, multimodal preprocessing is still per request: the HF processor receives `text=[input_text]`, and GLM flattens the result before restoring a `[1, sequence_length]` dimension for MRoPE. Continuous GPU batching happens later and does not add padding at this call site.

### How the mismatch was introduced

The GLM processor originally landed in [#8798](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/8798). At that point, both `input_ids` and `attention_mask` came directly from the HF processor, so they were aligned. Passing the processor mask to the GLM MRoPE helper was valid and preserved its support for padded batches.

[#26555](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26555) later added exact-ID restoration for pretokenized RL/VLM requests. The shared base processor began replacing the HF processor's `input_ids`, but the GLM consumer continued reading `attention_mask` from the old processor result. The two changes are independently reasonable; the bug is the missing ownership update between them.

### Reproduction

The tokenizer drift can be reproduced independently of the model backend:

```python
import torch
from transformers import AutoTokenizer

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash")
newline = tokenizer.encode("\n", add_special_tokens=False)
exact_ids = tokenizer.encode("hello", add_special_tokens=False) + newline + newline
retokenized_ids = tokenizer.encode(
    tokenizer.decode(exact_ids), add_special_tokens=False
)

assert len(retokenized_ids) == len(exact_ids) - 1

ids = torch.tensor([exact_ids])
retokenized_mask = torch.ones((1, len(retokenized_ids)), dtype=torch.long)
ids[0][retokenized_mask[0] == 1]  # IndexError: mask and tensor shapes differ
```

The server path requires:

1. `SGLANG_MM_AVOID_RETOKENIZE=1` (the default);
2. a request containing exact `input_ids` and raw image data;
3. a noncanonical token sequence whose decode/tokenize round trip changes length.

The original report observed the failure in GLM-5.3 long multi-turn vision RL at approximately 8K and 36K tokens. The linked reproduction reports the same workload completing after the one-line change.

### Expected behavior

Any token-aligned mask passed to MRoPE must correspond to the final `input_ids`.

At the current GLM call site, each processor invocation contains exactly one unpadded sequence. Passing `attention_mask=None` is therefore behavior-preserving: `get_rope_index_glm4v` creates `torch.ones_like(total_input_ids)`, which is identical to the processor mask when lengths agree and correctly follows the final exact IDs when they do not.

This is a general fix for models using `Glm4vImageProcessor`, but the framework-level invariant is broader: if `process_and_combine_mm_data` replaces `input_ids`, downstream code should not consume token-aligned fields from the old processor result without rebuilding them.

A regression test should cover noncanonical pretokenized IDs plus an image and verify both exact-ID preservation and MRoPE position generation. A canonical-ID case should also verify that positions are unchanged.

### Fix scope

#### Immediate GLM fix

At this call site, pass `attention_mask=None` to `get_rope_index_glm4v`. The helper then creates `torch.ones_like(total_input_ids)` from the final exact IDs.

This is safe under the current `Glm4vImageProcessor` contract:

- processing is one request at a time;
- `padding=True` with `text=[input_text]` does not add padding;
- later continuous batching and RL training batching happen after MRoPE preprocessing;
- when the tokenizations already match, the processor mask is also all ones, so behavior is unchanged.

The current fix in #36833 follows this approach. Mask support should remain in `get_rope_index_glm4v`; only this unpadded call site should stop forwarding a potentially stale mask.

#### Principle-level fix

`process_and_combine_mm_data` should make the final `input_ids` and all token-aligned metadata share the same provenance. If it replaces processor-generated IDs with exact client IDs, it should also rebuild or invalidate the corresponding `attention_mask` and any other token-aligned fields.

One possible interface is to return an aligned final mask alongside the final IDs instead of requiring model-specific processors to read it from the raw HF result:

```python
mm_items, input_ids, attention_mask, processor_output = (
    process_and_combine_mm_data(...)
)
```

For today's per-request unpadded path, that mask is simply `torch.ones_like(final_input_ids)`. If true padded processor batching is added later, the base layer can construct the mask from the final sequence lengths after rebuilding/padding the IDs.

The important invariant is:

```text
final input_ids and every token-aligned tensor must describe the same sequence
```

This would remove the same class of stale-metadata bugs from downstream multimodal processors rather than fixing each consumer separately.

### Environment

```text
Model: zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash
SGLANG_MM_AVOID_RETOKENIZE: 1 (default)
Affected current main: 512df615debca0240addeacedf19c28f0fc18c45
Affected #36507 head: 7fa1924c04487feffc3f5f111a424ec1f0b22362
Miles-branch fix currently tracked in: #36833
```

The exception occurs during CPU-side multimodal preprocessing, before model execution or continuous batching, so it is independent of the GPU and attention backend.

items.title: [Bug] Qwen3.8-Flash-Next W4A16 on A100 TP4: Marlin MoE invalid thread config; Triton MoE then hits QSA FA-CuTe capture failure
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest day-0 image.
- [x] This report includes environment info and reproduction parameters.
- [x] This is a bug report, not a general question.

### Summary

On 4x NVIDIA A100-40GB with TP4, the day-0 `qwen38flashnext` image can load the community W4A16 checkpoint of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next with PLE host offload and bundled NEXTN/MTP. Startup fails at CUDA-graph capture, but with two independent kernel failures depending on the MoE runner backend:

1. Default/auto MoE: `CompressedTensorsWNA16MarlinMoEMethod` throws `Invalid thread config` for the TP4 expert GEMM shape `MKN = [64, 2560, 320]`.
2. `--moe-runner-backend triton` selects `CompressedTensorsWNA16TritonMoE` successfully and avoids the Marlin error, but QSA sparse attention then falls into `flash_attn.cute` during CUDA-graph capture and fails with an MLIR `crd2idx` compilation error.

The second run also emits many Triton warnings similar to:

```text
Data race detected: `Logits(bx, position)` is written by multiple threads in loop (token,)
```

### Environment

```text
GPU: 4x NVIDIA A100-SXM4/PCIe 40GB (TP4)
Driver-visible model names: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB, NVIDIA A100-PCIE-40GB
Model: /data/ai/models/vllm/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16 (compressed-tensors W4A16)
Image: lmsysorg/sglang:qwen38flashnext
Image digest: sha256:4175343ed77bb05000ee5019b2dc3fa8999cd52edd6da7e5b75d23306c445c5f
CUDA in container: 13.0.3
TP: 4
Host RAM: 377 GiB (PLE offload fits comfortably)
```

### Reproduction

The model was mounted at `/models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16`. This is the minimum command structure used with Docker Compose:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16 \
  --ple-offload-embedding \
  --speculative-algorithm NEXTN \
  --speculative-num-steps 3 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
  --moe-runner-backend auto \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8888 \
  --tp 4 \
  --context-length 262144 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.95 \
  --attention-backend flashinfer \
  --chunked-prefill-size 16384 \
  --max-prefill-tokens 32768 \
  --max-running-requests 16 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs 16 \
  --cuda-graph-bs-prefill 4 8 16 32 64 128 256 512 1024 2048 4096 8192 16384 \
  --schedule-policy fcfs \
  --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --served-model-name Qwen3.8-Flash-Next \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --mamba-ssm-dtype float32 \
  --mamba-backend flashinfer \
  --mm-feature-transport cpu \
  --disable-custom-all-reduce
```

For the second failure, replace `--moe-runner-backend auto` with:

```bash
--moe-runner-backend triton
```

### Result 1 — default/auto: Marlin MoE shape/thread-config failure

Model and MTP weights load successfully. During decode CUDA-graph capture:

```text
[TP0] Using CompressedTensorsWNA16MarlinMoEMethod
...
Capturing batches (bs=16 avail_mem=2.10 GB):   0%| 0/12 [00:00<?, ?it/s]
tvm.error.InternalError: Failed at .../moe_wna16_marlin.cuh:747:
Invalid thread config: thread_m_blocks = 1, thread_k = -1, thread_n = -1,
num_threads = -1 for MKN = [64, 2560, 320] and num_bits = 4,
group_size = 128, has_act_order = 0, is_k_full = 1, has_zp = 0,
is_zp_float = 0, max_shared_mem = 166912
```

Relevant stack:

```text
fused_moe_triton/layer.py -> run_moe_core
compressed_tensors.py -> scheme.apply_weights
compressed_tensors_wNa16_moe.py -> fused_marlin_moe
moe_wna16_marlin.py -> module.moe_wna16_marlin_gemm
moe_wna16_marlin.cuh -> host::RuntimeCheck(is_valid_config(...))
```

Observations:

- `MKN = [64, 2560, 320]` appears to be one of the TP4-sharded expert GEMMs.
- The small `prob_n = 320` is not divisible by the 128-wide tile candidate, so both built-in small-batch configs are rejected.
- The error occurs before service readiness; there is no OOM.

### Result 2 — `--moe-runner-backend triton`: Marlin is bypassed, but QSA/FA-CuTe capture fails

Logs confirm the intended switch:

```text
Using CompressedTensorsWNA16TritonMoE (moe_runner_backend=triton)
```

There are also missing tuned-kernel notices for A100:

```text
Using default MoE kernel config. Performance might be sub-optimal!
Config file not found:
.../E=512,N=80,device_name=NVIDIA_A100-SXM4-40GB,dtype=int4_w4a16.json
.../E=512,N=80,device_name=NVIDIA_A100-SXM4-40GB,dtype=int4_w4a16_down.json
```

Weight loading and memory allocation succeed:

```text
Load weight end. type=Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration, mem usage=19.19 GB.
Load weight end. type=Qwen4ExpForCausalLMMTP, mem usage=1.78 GB.
Mamba Cache is allocated.
KV Cache is allocated. #tokens: 612672, K size: 3.51 GB, V size: 3.51 GB.
```

Then capture reaches bs=16 and crashes in QSA sparse attention:

```text
Capture target verify CUDA graph begin. backend=full, num_tokens_per_req=4, bs=[...]
Capturing batches (bs=16 avail_mem=2.43 GB): 0%| 0/12 [00:52<?, ?it/s]
...
qwen_sparse_attn_backend.py -> _forward_paged_attention -> flash_attn_varlen_func
flash_attn/cute/interface.py -> _flash_attn_fwd
cutlass._mlir...MLIRError: Operation creation failed:
error: unknown: unable to compute crd2idx with
  '!cute.layout<"(?):(?{i64 div=8})">' and '!cute.coord<"((?,?))">'
```

The traceback starts in the Qwen4Exp target-verify CUDA-graph path and passes through `QwenSparseAttnBackend.forward_extend`, so the second failure is independent of the MoE backend that successfully loaded.

### Workarounds considered

- `--moe-runner-backend triton` avoids the exact Marlin failure, but exposes the second QSA/FA-CuTe failure.
- Disabling decode CUDA graph may bypass capture, but has not yet been tested here and is expected to reduce decode performance.
- The official Flash-Next cookbook currently verifies H200/B200/B300/GB300/MI350X/MI355X; A100 and community W4A16 are outside the verified matrix, so this report is mainly about making the failure actionable and determining whether A100 TP4 can be supported or should fail fast with a clearer compatibility message.

### Request

1. Confirm whether `CompressedTensorsWNA16MarlinMoEMethod` can support the TP4-sharded Flash-Next expert GEMM shape (`prob_n = 320`), or whether it should fall back to Triton automatically for invalid Marlin shapes.
2. For the Triton MoE + QSA path, determine whether A100/SM80 can use classic FA2 for QSA instead of `flash_attn.cute`, or whether A100 should be explicitly unsupported/preflighted for this day-0 model.
3. If known, advice on the best supported A100 configuration for this W4A16 checkpoint, even if it requires disabling CUDA graphs.

items.title: [Feature] compute-mamba-ratio skill: plain-spec D is off the slot budget; admission clamp needs a +1 slot margin
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Motivation

Two sizing corrections for the `compute-mamba-ratio` skill (#32763, #32789), found while sizing GLM-5.3-Flash on 8×H100 (TP8 + `--enable-dp-attention` dp8, NEXTN `D=6`, `extra_buffer`, overlap on, image `0.0.0.dev1+g033446bb05`). This is feedback on the sizing guidance, not a bug report against the runtime.

#### 1. Plain spec: `D` is no longer a slot-pool cost — same accounting as the ReplaySSM caveat

The skill computes `r* = (S + D) · token_equiv · dcp / L` and pins `--max-mamba-cache-size = target_concurrency · S` (joint-solving `(S+D)` per request with spec).

On current main, plain EAGLE/NEXTN allocates the per-draft intermediate states in a dedicated buffer sized by `max_running_requests`, outside the slot pool:

- `memory_pool.py`: `intermediate_ssm_state_cache` shape `(layers, spec_state_size + 1, D, ...)`
- `kv_cache_configurator.py`: `mamba_spec_state_size=sizes.max_running_requests`

So the slot-pool cost per running request is `S`, and `D` is a fixed deduction from `rest` scaled by `max_running_requests` — exactly the treatment the skill already prescribes for ReplaySSM, but it applies to plain spec too. Using `(S+D)` overestimated the state pool ~2.2× at `L≈300K` in our case.

Boot-log evidence (per rank, dp8 so pools are /8):

```
Mamba Cache is allocated. max_mamba_cache_size: 30, conv_state size: 0.15GB, ssm_state size: 2.12GB intermediate_ssm_state_cache size: 2.87GB intermediate_conv_window_cache size: 0.20GB
```

`ssm_state 2.12 GiB / 31 = 68.4 MiB/slot`; `intermediate_ssm_state_cache 2.87 GiB = (6+1 reqs) × 6 drafts × 68.4 MiB` — sized by per-rank `max_running_requests`, not by slot count. The configurator's own clamp is `mmcs // S` (30 // 5 = 6/rank), which matched observed admission.

#### 2. The pin needs a +1 slot margin: chunked-prefill stash transiently allocates before freeing

With admission exactly at the clamp (6 running/rank × S=5 = 30/30 slots, all locked), the chunk-boundary stash (`cache_unfinished_req` → `prepare_for_caching_req` → `_alloc_mamba_slot`) allocates the donate slot before the old one is released. Transient demand is `running · S + 1`. `evict_for_alloc` cannot free anything (all slots belong to running requests), the assert fires, and the scheduler exits. Under round-robin DP load all 8 ranks hit it within one second, taking the whole server down. Deterministic for us: 48 concurrent 8K-in/1K-out requests crash; 16 concurrent never do.

<details>
<summary>Crash log (same on all 8 ranks)</summary>

```
[2026-08-29 07:48:03 DP0] Prefill batch, ... full token usage: 0.12, mamba usage: 1.00, #running-req: 4, ...
[2026-08-29 07:48:03 DP0] Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
  File ".../managers/scheduler.py", line 3151, in get_next_batch_to_run
    self.stash_chunked_request(self.chunked_req)
  File ".../mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py", line 927, in cache_unfinished_req
    cl = comp.prepare_for_caching_req(
  File ".../mem_cache/unified_cache/components/mamba_component.py", line 498, in _alloc_mamba_slot
    assert slot is not None, "Can not alloc mamba cache"
AssertionError: Can not alloc mamba cache
```

</details>

Suggested skill changes:

1. Add a caveat mirroring the ReplaySSM one: when the boot log shows a separate `intermediate_ssm_state_cache` allocation, use `D=0` in the slot math and account the buffer as a `rest` deduction driven by `max_running_requests`.
2. Change the pin recommendation to `--max-mamba-cache-size = target_concurrency · S + 1` (per attention-dp rank), or note that the configurator clamp sits exactly on the assert boundary.

Corrected sizing validated on the same deployment: pin 136 (17/rank = 3·S + 2 margin), `--max-running-requests 24`, rest to KV (per-rank KV tokens 359,680 → 889,536). 16× and 24× concurrent 330K-token requests all completed correctly, zero restarts.

### Related resources

- #32763, #32789 (`compute-mamba-ratio` skill)
- `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py` (`intermediate_ssm_state_cache`), `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/kv_cache_configurator.py` (`mamba_spec_state_size`), `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_cache/components/mamba_component.py` (`_alloc_mamba_slot`)

items.title: [Bug] MiMo-V2.5: any request with audio hangs the whole server under --enable-dp-attention (audio encoder reduces over the wrong TP group)
items.body:
### Describe the bug

Serving **MiMo-V2.5** (`MiMoV2ForCausalLM`) with DP attention — the configuration the model effectively mandates on an 8-GPU node, since its fused `qkv_proj` requires effective attention TP = 4:

```
--tp 8 --dp 2 --enable-dp-attention --enable-dp-lm-head --mm-enable-dp-encoder --quantization fp8
```

any request **containing audio** permanently hangs the whole server. Text-only and video-without-audio requests work fine.

| case | result |
|---|---|
| text only | ✅ |
| video without audio | ✅ |
| **audio (any request carrying an audio item)** | ❌ hangs 600 s, then the server dies |
| everything after that | ❌ connection refused |

Server log at the moment of death:

```
[PG ID 4 PG GUID 23(attention_tp:device) Rank 3] Process group watchdog thread terminated with exception:
[Rank 3] Watchdog caught collective operation timeout: WorkNCCL(SeqNum=14708, OpType=_ALLGATHER_BASE,
NumelIn=38144, NumelOut=152576, Timeout(ms)=600000) ran for 600083 milliseconds before timing out.
```

followed by gloo `Connection closed by peer` on the sibling ranks. Reproduced twice independently (official FP8 weights and a bf16 export) on 8×H200; identical signature both times.

### Root cause

`AudioEncoderAttention` builds its `VisionAttention` without `use_data_parallel` / `use_dp_attention_reduce` (`python/sglang/srt/models/mimo_audio.py:503`). Consequently:

- The audio encoder's attention weights **are sharded over the attention-TP group** — `_remap_audio_tokenizer_state_dict` slices by `attn_tp_rank`/`attn_tp_size` (`mimo_audio.py:1122-1173`), and `VisionAttention` defaults to `tp_size = attn_tp_size` (`layers/attention/vision.py:1072`).
- But its output projection's `RowParallelLinear` reduces over the **full TP group**: with `use_dp_attention_reduce=False` the reduce path takes `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce` (`layers/linear.py:1666`) — 8 ranks, not 4.
- The audio encoder is only entered by ranks whose local batch actually has audio items: `general_mm_embed_routine` skips modalities with zero items (`managers/mm_utils.py:420`, `if len(items) != 0:`).

So when one DP group's batch carries audio and the other's does not, the audio-bearing group issues `encoder_layers × all_reduce` on the full-TP communicator that the other group never joins. The TP communicator desynchronizes and every subsequent collective piles up behind it.

The watchdog blames `attention_tp` only because that is the sole c10d-instrumented communicator in this setup: the full TP group runs through custom-allreduce/pynccl (no watchdog), while `attention_tp` falls through to `torch.distributed.all_gather_into_tensor` (`distributed/parallel_state.py:2596-2608`, `1246-1248`). The reported `_ALLGATHER_BASE` (`NumelIn=38144, NumelOut=152576` = 1 row × vocab 152576 / attn_tp 4) is the last-token logits gather of the audio request's prefill (`layers/logits_processor.py:926`) — enqueued behind the wedged all-reduce, never executed.

Two further consequences worth noting:

1. **Even when every DP group happens to have audio items, the numerics are wrong**: the full-TP reduce sums partials from unrelated DP groups' audio batches.
2. Video is immune precisely because the ViT honors `--mm-enable-dp-encoder` (`models/mimo_vl.py:261` → `use_data_parallel=True`, no collectives); the audio encoder is not wired to either flag.

Every other multimodal encoder in the tree already passes one of the two flags (`qwen3_vl.py:161`, `kimi_k25.py:130`, `minimax_vl_common.py:108`, `mimo_vl.py:300`); the audio encoder is the one that was missed. `mimo_v2_asr.py` inherits the same defect through `AudioEncoderMixin`.

Note `sglang`'s own `--watchdog-timeout` does not help — the 600 s timeout is `ProcessGroupNCCL`'s collective timeout, not the scheduler watchdog.

### Reproduction

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5 --trust-remote-code \
  --tp 8 --dp 2 --enable-dp-attention --enable-dp-lm-head --mm-enable-dp-encoder \
  --quantization fp8 --attention-backend fa3 --mm-attention-backend fa3
# then send any /v1/chat/completions request whose content includes an audio item
# (audio_only, or video with an audio track). With dp 2, the request lands in one
# DP group and the hang is immediate and deterministic in our runs.
```

### Environment

8×H200 (141 GB), sglang 0.5.18 (also verified the defective code path is unchanged on current `main` @ 97781eb7f), torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, fa3 attention backend.

items.title: [Bug] Qwen3.8-Flash-Next + NEXTN full decode graph: repeated dual-rank invalid-probability asserts on GB10
items.body:
## Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues and PRs but found no exact report for this model, `full` decode graph backend, stack, and hardware combination.
- [ ] The bug persists in the latest SGLang version. The affected day-zero image is pinned to `d91c3682`; a current-main rebuild has not yet been validated on this two-node system.
- [x] Environment information and a synthetic reproduction/stress harness are included.
- [x] This report is in English and concerns a reproducible serving crash.

## Describe the bug

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4 serving on two NVIDIA DGX Spark GB10 (`sm_121`) nodes with TP2 and NEXTN/EAGLE repeatedly aborts both tensor-parallel ranks under long/chunked workloads when the decode CUDA graph backend is `full`.

The first explicit CUDA error is:

```text
TensorCompare.cu:109: Assertion `probability tensor contains either `inf`, `nan` or element < 0` failed.
```

This is followed by `CUDA error: device-side assert triggered`, a scheduler stack surfacing through `eagle_worker_v2._draft_extend_for_prefill` / `ForwardBatch.init_new` / `_compute_mrope_positions_extend`, NCCL/process-group failure, NVIDIA Xid 43 on both nodes, and container restart.

Five post-patch production incidents occurred on both TP ranks at the same timestamps. Docker reported `OOMKilled=false` for every incident.

### Key A/B result

Before mitigation, runtime configuration was:

```text
cuda_graph_config.decode.backend='full'
cuda_graph_config.prefill.backend='disabled'
speculative_algorithm='EAGLE'
speculative_num_steps=3
speculative_eagle_topk=1
speculative_num_draft_tokens=4
```

Changing only from `--disable-prefill-cuda-graph` to full `--disable-cuda-graph` retained NEXTN/EAGLE but disabled both graph phases. A synthetic stress canary then passed:

- 52/52 non-streaming requests
- 2,357,058 prompt tokens
- maximum individual prompt: 93,781 tokens
- 9 synthetic-image requests
- 24 concurrent long-context requests
- two forced 256-token generations after approximately 90K-word prompts
- zero scheduler/CUDA errors, zero new Xid 43 events, zero container restarts on both ranks

This strongly implicates an interaction between speculative decoding and the **full decode CUDA-graph path**. It does not prove that `_compute_mrope_positions_extend` is the origin, because CUDA reports errors asynchronously.

## Reproduction

### Model and launch flags

```bash
sglang serve --model-path /models/qwen3.8-flash-next-nvfp4 \
  --tp-size 2 --nnodes 2 --node-rank '<0-or-1>' \
```

items.title: [Bug] --enable-symm-mem: all TP schedulers deadlock silently in ncclCommWindowRegister (blocking UDS recvmsg, no timeout) when the symmetric-memory pool grows at runtime
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

**TL;DR:** with `--enable-symm-mem` on a multi-rank TP engine, every TP scheduler process can deadlock **permanently and silently** inside `ncclCommWindowRegister`. The trigger is routine: whenever the symmetric-memory mempool grows by a new segment at runtime (which `use_symmetric_memory` context exits then register with the communicator), all ranks enter NCCL's symmetric window registration together, and the fd-exchange rendezvous inside NCCL (2.29.7) can lose its Unix-domain-socket message. Every rank then blocks in a **timeout-less `recvmsg`** while every NCCL UDS proxy thread sits idle in `poll()`. Nothing is ever logged, `/health` keeps returning 200 (it does not touch the scheduler), GPUs sit at 0% utilization, and the server serves nothing until SGLang's scheduler watchdog SIGQUITs it ~30+ minutes later. We hit this repeatedly in production (15 watchdog kills across 10 engines in two days) and then reproduced it in ~40 minutes on a test node with the stacks below.

This is the failure mode class the code itself worries about: registration is driven by *rank-local* allocator behavior but performed as a *collective*, from the hot forward path, with no timeout and no logging (`python/sglang/srt/distributed/device_communicators/pynccl_allocator.py`, `_register_segments_for_comm` / `nccl_allocator_register_segments_with_comm`).

#### Symptom fingerprint (what an affected operator sees)

- The scheduler stops between one batch log line and the next — no error, no traceback. `forward_ct` freezes with a batch in flight, so the watchdog fires 1×–1.5× `--watchdog-timeout` later and kills the server; a restart fully recovers.
- `/health` stays 200 throughout (with health-endpoint generation disabled it never touches the scheduler); `/get_server_info` hangs. Load balancers keep routing to a dead replica.
- All TP ranks freeze within the same second with identical state; GPU utilization is 0% and power is at idle for the whole hang (no kernel is resident — the wait is CPU-side).
- The watchdog dump's `leaked_full_pages` / `leaked_mamba_pages` sets look alarming but are a red herring: `dump_info` applies the idle-only pool invariant to a busy scheduler (no `uncached` term), so the in-flight batch's own pages/slots are printed as "leaked". This misdirected our investigation for a long time — a diagnostics fix worth making separately.

#### Captured stacks (all four TP ranks byte-identical, py-spy + gdb, live hang)

Python (py-spy; ranks TP0–TP3 all identical, taken mid-hang):

```
Thread (active): "MainThread"
    _register_segments_for_comm (sglang/srt/distributed/device_communicators/pynccl_allocator.py:319)
    __exit__ (pynccl_allocator.py:294)                 # use_symmetric_memory context exit
    forward (sglang/srt/layers/linear.py:1622)         # RowParallelLinear, mid-chunked-prefill
    ...model layers...
    _execute_extend (runner/eager_runner.py:352)
    forward (model_runner.py:1583)
    forward_batch_generation (tp_worker.py:618)
    run_batch (managers/scheduler.py)
    event_loop_overlap (managers/scheduler.py)
```

Native (gdb, same thread; NCCL 2.29.7 with symbols):

```
#0  recvmsg ()                                         libc
#1  ncclIpcSocketRecvMsg                               nccl os/linux_ipcsocket.cc:140
#2  ncclProxyCallBlockingUDS (type=9, respFd wanted)   proxy.cc:1265
#3  ncclProxyClientGetFdBlocking (proxyRank=<peer>)    proxy.cc:1288
#4  symMemoryImportAndMapSegmentHandle                 dev_runtime.cc:257
#5  symMemoryImportAndMapSegmentsForRank               dev_runtime.cc:287
#6  symMemoryMapLsaTeam                                dev_runtime.cc:328
#7  symMemoryObtain (numSegments=1, size=2097152)      dev_runtime.cc:604
#8  ncclDevrWindowRegisterInGroup                      dev_runtime.cc:897
#9  ncclCommGroupRegisterSymmetric                     group.cc:264
#10 ncclAsyncJobMain / groupLaunch / ncclGroupEndInternal   group.cc
#14 ncclCommWindowRegister                             dev_runtime.cc:1368
#15 nccl_allocator_register_segments_with_comm         (sglang's embedded C in pynccl_allocator.py)
```

Meanwhile, in the same gdb dumps, every rank's `ncclProxyService` (proxy.cc:1780) and `ncclProxyServiceUDS` (proxy.cc:2000) threads are idle in `poll()` — four clients blocked in `recvmsg` waiting for an fd reply, four proxy servers seeing no request. The registered segment was a single fresh 2 MiB mempool segment.

With `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=REG`, the boot that hung showed 107 completed `register comm` rounds, exactly paired across all 4 devices (dozens of them post-warmup — runtime mempool growth is routine, e.g. when a long prompt's chunk allocates larger activations after an idle period). The hang was round #108: the round's `register` lines never appeared. So the collective call pairing was correct; the rendezvous inside NCCL deadlocked. Each runtime registration round is a dice roll.

The root defect may ultimately be in NCCL 2.29.x's symmetric-window fd exchange (we're happy to cross-file with NVIDIA if useful), but SGLang owns the exposure: registering rank-local, unpredictable mempool growth from inside the forward pass, collectively, with no timeout, no logging, and no failure surface.

### Reproduction

Single 4×B200 node, TP4/EP4, GLM-5.3-Flash (glm-5-next branch; the mechanism is model-independent — any model whose forward allocates through `use_symmetric_memory` should do):

```
sglang serve --model-path zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --tp-size 4 --ep-size 4 \
  --enable-symm-mem --enable-nccl-nvls --pre-warm-nccl \
  --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --max-running-requests 12 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm \
  --watchdog-timeout 1800
```

Traffic shape that triggers it (both with and without speculative decoding; also seen with `--enable-mixed-chunk`): alternate idle gaps (20–600 s) with bursts of 2–4 short requests generating 500–1500 tokens each, plus one 90k–200k-token prefill fired into the running decodes. In production the hang struck ~10 engines over two days under organic agentic traffic; on the test node this loop reproduced it in ~40 minutes. The deadlocked registration fires when a burst after an idle gap makes the symm-mem mempool grow — `NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=REG` makes the rounds visible, and the hang is the round whose `register` lines never print.

Diagnosis tips for anyone else hitting this: `/health` 200 + `/get_server_info` hanging + all-GPU 0% util is the signature; the built-in watchdog's `pyspy_dump_schedulers()` fails with `Failed to copy Py_Version symbol` unless the container has `SYS_PTRACE` (worth documenting / adding to deploy templates — with the capability, the watchdog dump would have named this stack on day one).

### Suggested fixes

1. **Give the registration path a timeout + loud failure**: a bounded wait around `ncclCommWindowRegister` in `nccl_allocator_register_segments_with_comm` (or at least a log line before/after) would convert a silent 30-minute outage into an immediate, attributable crash.
2. **Avoid collective registration from the hot path**: pre-size the symm-mem mempool at startup and fail loudly on growth, or coordinate rounds explicitly (all ranks agree on "we register N segments now" at a point outside the forward).
3. `nccl_free_plug` resets *all* segment tracking and per-comm registration indices when any single segment is freed — under memory pressure this can desynchronize future registration counts across ranks; it should remove only the freed segment's state.
4. Cross-file with NCCL: `ncclProxyClientGetFdBlocking`'s UDS request/response (proxy.cc:1265/1288) appears to lose its message when all ranks of a communicator register concurrently; `ncclIpcSocketRecvMsg` then blocks forever.

Until then, our operational guidance is simply "do not enable `--enable-symm-mem` on multi-rank TP": removing the flag removes the code path entirely (confirmed by an A/B soak — same traffic, no registrations, no hangs).

### Environment

- SGLang: image `lmsysorg/sglang@sha256:39b03ac700333f7a23ab1c0a387bf57b828b5a5b8651c389a0c9188dc2dd367b` (source rev `f13cb6f6a7`, glm-5-next branch; `pynccl_allocator.py` registration logic is unchanged on current `main`)
- NCCL: 2.29.7 · torch 2.13.0+cu130 · CUDA 13.0.3 · driver on B200 (SM100), 4×GPU per engine, single node
- Python 3.12.3, Ubuntu 24.04 host, docker with `--ipc host`
- Flags as above; NVLS enabled; hang observed both with `--speculative-algorithm NEXTN` and without; with and without `--enable-mixed-chunk`

items.title: [GB10] Long prefill (>40k tokens) exhausts unified memory and silently kills the worker rank — no traceback, no OOM record; cross-stack control passes at 54k
items.body:
## Summary
On 2x DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121, TP=2, 121.7 GB unified memory per node), GLM-5.3-Flash prefills above roughly 40k tokens drive **host/unified memory on the worker node to its ceiling**, and somewhere between 54k and 62k tokens the worker rank dies with no traceback, no CUDA error, and no OOM record. The head then hangs on a collective and self-terminates.

This is chunked prefill (`--chunked-prefill-size 8192`), so per-step token counts are bounded — but measured memory grows with **total prompt length**, not chunk size, which suggests something in the prefill path retains per-token state across chunks.

## Measured
Config: SGLang @ `xinyuan/glm-5.3-flash-support` (aa8c950a3) + our fp8-KV patches (#36904), DFLASH speculative (D=5), `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, `--mem-fraction-static 0.92`, `--max-running-requests 8`, `--max-mamba-cache-size 40 --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16`, context 131072, KV pool 244,288 tokens.

Single request, needle-in-haystack prompt, `enable_thinking: false`, `max_tokens: 100`:

| prompt tokens | result | worker host memory (spark-2, of 124.6 GB) |
|---|---|---|
| ~32k | PASS (recall correct) | not sampled |
| ~40k | PASS but ~10 min wall (client timed out at 600 s; server kept generating) | **121.3 GB peak** |
| ~62k (on a 262144-context variant, fraction 0.93) | **worker container gone**, head hung then killed itself | not sampled |

Head-side symptom at the death:
```
[rank1] ProcessGroupNCCL ... Received a dump signal due to a collective timeout from rank 1
[TP1] Scheduler hit an exception: RuntimeError: ... gloo/transport/tcp/pair.cc:537
      Read error [10.10.10.1]:51085: Connection reset by peer
Received sigquit from a child process.
```
Docker reports `OOMKilled=false ExitCode=0 FinishedAt=0001-01-01T00:00:00Z` for the dead worker — i.e. the container's own state record is incoherent, consistent with the process being reaped outside docker's accounting rather than exiting.

Once the request is aborted and containers are removed, memory returns immediately (121.3 GB → 4.5 GB), so this is live allocation during prefill, not a leak that persists.

## Cross-stack control on the SAME hardware, same night
We ran a different serving stack on these exact two nodes (vLLM-based, EXL3 4bpw weights, fp8 KV, DFlash2 drafter, MLA/drafter KV page-sharing): identical needle prompts at **34,840 and 54,040 tokens both PASSED**, worker alive, peak host memory 119.3 GB. So the hardware and the fabric sustain 54k-token prefills; the failure is specific to this serving path.

## Why this may matter beyond our rig
Silent worker death on long prefill has been reported independently on GB10 with a different quantization (NVFP4 KV, ~6k tokens) and was assumed to be quant-specific. Our data falsifies that scoping: it reproduces on fp8_e4m3 KV at a higher threshold, so prompt length looks like the governing variable, not KV dtype.

## Asks
1. Is any prefill-path buffer expected to scale with **total** sequence length rather than chunk size on the DSA/tilelang path (indexer top-k workspaces, sparse index buffers, radix bookkeeping)?
2. Would a lower `--mem-fraction-static` plus smaller `--chunked-prefill-size` be the supported mitigation, or is there a bound we should be setting explicitly? (We are testing 2048/0.85 tonight and will post the result either way.)
3. On unified-memory parts, is there an intended guard that fails the request instead of the process when host memory is exhausted? A request-level error would turn a node kill into a retry.

Happy to run instrumented probes — we have the rig, the harness, and both stacks side by side.

Env: 2x DGX Spark GB10 (sm_121, aarch64), CUDA 13, TP=2/nnodes=2, dual-rail CX-7 RoCE, SGLang @ aa8c950a3 + PR #36904. Recipe/ladder: https://github.com/beastllama/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2-SGLang-2x-DGX-Spark
Related: #36889 (mamba cap), #36904 (fp8 KV), #36548 (DFLASH concurrency correctness on GB10).

items.title: [Bug] Prefill input logprobs are served from the wrong request when a batch member is retracted or finished
items.body:
### Describe the bug

In `process_batch_result_prefill`, the branch that skips finished-in-a-mixed-batch and retracted requests does not advance `logprob_pt`, so every later request in the same batch reads a shifted slice of the flat input-logprob array and is served **another request's prompt logprobs**.

The flat array holds one block per request in batch order regardless of whether that request asked for logprobs. That is why `_apply_prefill_logprobs` advances the cursor outside its `return_logprob` guard ([`batch_result_processor.py:522`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/batch_result_processor.py#L522)):

```python
        if req.return_logprob:
            self.logprob_result_processor.add_logprob_return_values(...)
        logprob_pt += num_input_logprobs
        return logprob_pt
```

The producer agrees: `logits_processor.py` builds `extend_logprob_pruned_lens_cpu` by appending `extend_len - start_len` for every sequence in the batch, using the same formula the consumer uses in `calculate_num_input_logprobs`.

But the skip at [`batch_result_processor.py:307-313`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/batch_result_processor.py#L307-L313) steps over a request without stepping the cursor:

```python
                if (
                    req.finished() and req.inflight_middle_chunks <= 0
                ) or req.is_retracted:
                    # Decode req in a mixed batch, or a retracted req. Keep an
                    # aborted middle chunk in the chunked branch long enough to
                    # drain its accounting without streaming it.
                    continue
```

`logprob_pt` is initialized at line 286 and advanced only at lines 344 and 374, both after this `continue`.

Nothing raises. The assertion in `logprob_result_processor.py` checks the slice **length**, not its offset, and the shift is always backwards, so it never runs off the end. The diagnostic signature is that `input_top_logprobs_val[i]` is indexed per request and stays correct while `input_token_logprobs` is sliced by the cursor and is wrong.

The disaggregated prefill loop already handles exactly this. `disaggregation/prefill.py:703` defines `advance_logprob_pt()` and calls it on each of its skip paths at lines 721, 789 and 797.

Scope: this bites when the skipped request itself requested input logprobs (`logprob_start_len >= 0`). With the default `-1` its block is zero rows and the skip is harmless. Overlap scheduling is on by default and retraction is ordinary under KV pressure, so no unusual flag is required.

### Reproduction

Driving the real `process_batch_result_prefill` on CPU with two prefill requests, the first retracted, `extend_input_len_per_req=[2, 3]` and `extend_logprob_start_len_per_req=[0, 0]`, over a flat array of `[-1.0, -2.0, -30.0, -31.0, -32.0]`:

```
expected (active request's own block)  [None, -30.0, -31.0]
actual                                 [None,  -1.0,  -2.0]   <- the retracted request's values
```

I have a regression test that reproduces this, written against the existing `test_batch_result_processor_hidden_states.py` harness and registered as `register_cpu_ci(est_time=2, suite="base-a-test-cpu")`, so it needs no GPU. It fails on `main` and passes with the cursor advanced. I will open a PR with the fix and that test shortly and link it here.

Related but distinct, so neither covers this path:
- [#34153](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34153) applies the same "consume the slice, skip the attach" idea to the `req.to_finish` path, which routes through the normal branch rather than this skip.
- [#36724](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36724) adds a new `deferred_mm_abort` branch immediately above this `continue` and advances the cursor there, leaving this one unchanged.
- [#32103](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32103) and [#32089](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/32089) describe the hidden-states analog and both cite this logprob path as already correct.

### Environment

`python3 -m sglang.check_env` does not run on a CPU-only host. [`check_env.py:583-594`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/check_env.py#L583-L594) is an `if/elif` chain over `is_cuda_v2()/is_hip()/is_npu()/is_musa()/is_mps()` with no `else`, so `env` is never bound and it exits with `NameError: name 'env' is not defined`. Reporting that separately. Environment collected by hand:

```
sglang commit: 0df69849ba
Python:        3.12.13
OS:            Linux-6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2-x86_64-with-glibc2.43
PyTorch:       2.13.0+cpu
transformers:  5.12.1
CUDA available: False
```

The affected code is pure Python request accounting in the scheduler and is exercised by the CPU test suite, so no accelerator is needed to reproduce it.

items.title: [Prefix Cache / Hybrid] Branch reuse silently collapses under LRU pressure when (kv_pool_tokens / chunked_prefill_size) > max_mamba_cache_size
items.body:
I've been characterizing Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 serving on a single RTX PRO 6000 (sm_120, 96 GB, TP=1, `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.17-cu130`, `--enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-size 150 --hicache-write-policy write_through`) under agentic workloads, and ran into a failure mode that I could eventually reproduce deterministically and turn on and off with single flags. Reporting it because #22326 anticipated exactly this capacity question and explicitly left it open ("assumes older checkpoints evict quickly when newer requests arrive, but this isn't guaranteed").

The observation: requests that share a prefix with a cached sequence but diverge mid-way (context compaction rewrites, session branches — the normal shape of agent traffic) go from a ~40k-token prefix hit to a 0-token hit, with no error and no log signal. Exact repeats keep hitting, so the regression is invisible unless you watch branch requests specifically. TTFT for the affected requests jumps from ~0.3 s to full cold prefill (~15 s at 80k in my probe; ~55 s at 190k).

Mechanism, as far as I can tell from reading the code and confirming with counters: interior mamba checkpoints are only created at chunked-prefill boundaries (`cache_unfinished_req` inserts once per chunk and donates the state), so checkpoint spacing along a cached chain equals `chunked_prefill_size`. A branch match needs the checkpoint at the divergence point, and KV+mamba are gated jointly — KV can be 100% resident and the match is still rejected if the mamba checkpoint is gone. On match, only the last node's mamba state is MRU-refreshed (`mamba_lru_list.reset_node_mru(last_node)`), so interior checkpoints age out under any sustained load. That gives a capacity criterion:

```
checkpoint demand ≈ kv_pool_tokens / chunked_prefill_size
demand > max_mamba_cache_size  =>  branch reuse collapses under LRU pressure
```

I tested the criterion from both sides on one box. Probe: build six distinct 80k-token chains, then issue a fresh branch request forking the oldest chain at its midpoint (~40k). `mamba_used/available/evictable` gauges from `/metrics` conserve to the pool size throughout, which is how I verified saturation.

| config | slots | kv_pool/cps | branch hit | pool at probe |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| cps=8192, fp32 | 165 | 433,919/8192 = 53 | 32,768 | evictable peak 44 |
| cps=2048, fp32 | 165 | 433,919/2048 = 212 | **0** | saturated, avail=5 |
| cps=2048, `--mamba-track-interval 8192` | 165 | 212 | 0 (byte-identical run) | saturated |
| cps=2048, `--mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16` | 325 | 212 | 32,768 | avail ≥111 |

Three things I'd flag from this:

1. The collapse follows the criterion, not the workload. Doubling the state pool (bf16) with everything else fixed makes it disappear; halving checkpoint spacing (cps 8192→2048) with everything else fixed makes it appear. Hit lengths are exactly cps-quantized throughout (32,768 = 16×2048, 38,912 = 19×2048), which also confirms the spacing claim.
2. `--mamba-track-interval` does not participate: setting it to 8192 changed nothing, run-for-run identical. As documented it's decode-side only. So today the *only* knob controlling prefill checkpoint density is `chunked_prefill_size` — a knob operators tune for prefill/decode interference. Lowering cps to protect TBT under concurrency silently pushes the engine across the criterion. That coupling is the actual footgun, and it's why I think the `prefill_cache_interval` idea from #22326 deserves to be revived: it's the missing independent knob.
3. At saturation the damage is broader than branches: cold chains lose their tail states too, so even exact-repeat requests for not-recently-touched sequences drop to 0 (observed on 2 of 5 chains in the saturated runs). The usual "exact repeats always hit" intuition only holds while the pool has headroom.

For what it's worth, this isn't a synthetic-only concern: serving 10 concurrent agent sessions (SWE-bench-style, 30–200k contexts) with cps=2048 on the same hardware, I've measured the mamba pool at 0.84–0.97 usage in steady state — the criterion regime is where agentic serving actually lives. Also possibly relevant to the `mamba_full_memory_ratio` discussion in #25993: with hicache enabled the derived pool on this box drops 165→147, and with EAGLE on top it drops to 70, so the criterion tightens twice before any user tuning happens.

Concrete asks, in increasing order of effort:

1. **A startup warning when the criterion is crossed.** At boot the engine already logs how the mamba pool caps `max_running_requests`; one more line when `kv_pool_tokens / chunked_prefill_size > max_mamba_cache_size` would name the coupling before an operator discovers it via TTFT spikes. A few lines, no behavior change — I can send this PR if you want it.
2. **A counter for mamba-gated match rejections.** When a branch match is rejected because the checkpoint is missing (KV present, mamba absent), nothing distinguishes it from a genuinely cold request today. A metric (or a debug-level log) would make the failure mode observable in production.
3. **Revive `prefill_cache_interval` from #22326.** Checkpoint density should have its own knob instead of riding on `chunked_prefill_size`; the capacity criterion above is the sizing rule that proposal said was missing ("assumes older checkpoints evict quickly … this isn't guaranteed" — measured: it isn't, and what gets evicted is exactly what branch reuse needs). With an independent interval, operators can tune cps for prefill/decode interference and checkpoint density for reuse, separately.

Happy to share the probe (~150-line standalone script against `/generate` + `/metrics`) and raw per-request JSONL for all four configs, or to rerun with different settings if that helps. I'm aware this is one box, one model family, synthetic chains; the numbers above are per-config single runs, but the on/off behavior reproduced every time I ran it.
